context:
Goal: your Mac coordinator starts its lane sessions with no press from you.
Problem (goal): the desktop app's start tool starts a session with no card only on a turn you typed, so a coordinator cannot use it on its own turns.
Based on (measured): Mac probes 4 and 5, 2026-11-06, Claude Code 2.1.296. The start tool showed no card on your typed turn (3 of 3), but was refused on a wake turn even after allow. claude -p run by a session showed no card, and 7 of 9 runs answered (2 failed on a login-refresh clash). With --permission-mode auto it wrote a file with no denials. The run does not show in the session list.
Based on (assumed): the no-card reading holds if your Mac coordinators run in bypass permissions mode, as the probe session may have. In default mode, starting claude -p asks you to press; in auto mode it is unmeasured.
Departs from: decision lanes-start-as-agents, where each Mac lane start is one press — becomes the pick.
Meanwhile: PR #1339 stays held; the c107 lane builds your pick.
holds: How the Mac coordinator starts lane sessions.
home: coordinator: hand the Mac lane-start question to a session on your Mac

lastAnswer.note: unsure why you think these are the only options. maybe i need to handle this part in a local session? your assumptions are just all wrong and all over the place. what do you think you're even trying to solve here anymore?

options.gain: No card and no typing. Each lane keeps its own session and transcript, as your Nov 4 ruling wants (item 168).
options.how: The coordinator starts each Mac lane with claude -p --permission-mode auto in the lane's own worktree, and sends each next step with --resume.
options.label: CLI lanes
options.lose: The lane does not show in your desktop session list, and you cannot type to it there. It is not live between steps, so the coordinator drives every turn. A login clash can fail a start, so the coordinator retries. Lanes run in auto mode.

options.gain: No press, and the coordinator sees each one live.
options.how: Lanes run as background agents inside the coordinator.
options.label: Background agents
options.lose: Goes against your item 168 ruling: a lane is a session. A lane ends when the coordinator's session ends, and you cannot open it as its own session.

options.gain: Lanes are live, visible on claude.ai, take messages, and run off your machine.
options.how: A cloud coordinator starts cloud lanes for work that does not need the Mac. Mac-bound lanes (iOS simulator, local files) still use a or b.
options.label: Cloud coordinator
options.lose: Two paths to keep. Mac-bound work still needs a or b.

reply: Closed at 17:10 CST. The goal was that a coordinator on your Mac starts lane sessions without you pressing anything. A cloud lane on another account was guessing at your Mac through probes you pasted, which is the wrong setup. A session on your Mac can see its own tools and test directly. The coordinator decides that hand-off and comes back with a fresh item only if a pick is still needed.
title: How should your Mac coordinator start lane sessions with no press from you?
why: Only a keeps each lane its own session with no press, measured on your Mac.
